subject: Redwood vs hyperscaler — capacity pathways & next benchmarks
messages:

Date: 2027-02-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro + capacity questions

Thanks for the call this morning — quick follow-up items from our side:
- Primary requirement: predictable daytime capacity for our ETL/feature-generation windows (9am-5pm ET) with the ability to burst for nightly large-batch embedding jobs.
- Workloads: user-facing chat (p50 targeted <= 120ms token latency), synchronous reranking, and intermittent 200k+ embedding batches.
- Procurement/security: we'll need SOC 2 evidence, audit-log retention policy, and a short note on where KV cache and user data are stored (VPC tenancy or shared).

What would help next: a short matrix comparing Redwood dedicated reserved pools vs GCP committed NVIDIA L4 instances (incl. throughput guarantees, expected p95 under contention, and recovery/fallback behavior). Also share an outline of a POC benchmark we can run — minimal infra footprint, we can provide a sample corpus.

If possible, include ballpark committed pricing and what burst capacity looks like (how much overhead for 2x day peaks). We'll loop procurement once we have that.

Thanks,

Asha

MedLytics
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha@medlytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood vs hyperscaler — capacity pathways & next benchmarks

Hi Asha — great talking earlier. High level response and immediate next steps below. I've attached a concise POC plan and an SLA comparison PDF for quick review (see attachments).

TL;DR: Redwood Dedicated gives you a reserved GPU pool with predictable throughput and automatic degraded-mode fallbacks (lower-cost variants + region failover). Hyperscaler committed instances offer strong per-VM guarantees but you retain more of the orchestration burden (and less flexibility on automatic model fallbacks).

What we'll include in the matrix (short):
- Guaranteed concurrent sessions at target latency (we'll measure p50/p95 for chat and embed throughput)
- Recovery and fallbacks (how we route to lower-capacity variants or alternate regions)
- Operational ownership (who patches, who manages autoscaling, who owns warm KV cache)
- Billing model for reserved vs burst usage (how we count token units when model changes or fallback triggers)

Proposed POC benchmark (week-of 2/22):
1) We provision a small dedicated pool sized to your daytime concurrency profile (we'll propose sizing after you send a 48hr traffic sample).
2) Run three tests: steady-state low-latency chat (concurrency ladder), high-throughput embedding batch (200k batch), and fault-injection (simulate node loss).
3) Metrics: p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, failure rate, time-to-fallback, and cost per 1M tokens under each test.

Action items for MedLytics: share 48hr traffic sample (token count by hour), preferred test window, and any data residency constraints.

Ben will follow up with a technical runbook and the benchmark artifacts. I'll get pricing ranges for reserved terms (6/12/24 months) with delta to on-demand hyperscaler pricing.

If procurement wants to pre-review contract language, loop them in and we'll provide a one-page carveout for auditing and data controls.

Best,
Kimberly

--

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Menon <asha@medlytics.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-02-15T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood vs hyperscaler — technical bench details and artifacts

Hi Asha / Kim — attaching the benchmark artifacts and a short runbook (attachment: redwood-poc-benchmarks.tar.gz). A few technical clarifications for the POC so we size the pool correctly:
- For chat: if you target ~120ms p50 token latency, we assume model footprint and KV cache will be hot for 90% of requests. Please indicate mean tokens per request (we used 60 tokens as a baseline).
- For embeddings: parallelization strategy matters — we'll provide a small launcher script that runs batches at variable parallelism so you can find the sweet spot between GPU util and network IO.
- Recovery/fallback: Redwood will automatically route to a compatible lower-cost quantized variant when a node is lost; this preserves availability but will slightly affect quality. We will capture quality deltas in the POC.
- Concurrency guarantees: with Dedicated we reserve capacity and expose a per-tenant concurrency limit; for hyperscaler reserved instances you'd typically see a VM-level limit and you'd need extra orchestration for seamless failover.

Test matrix (what we'll measure):
- p50/p95 token latency (chat)
- tokens/sec sustained at target concurrency (chat + batch mix)
- time-to-fallback and error-rate under node loss
- cost per 1M tokens at measured throughput (we'll compute for 6/12/24 month reserved pricing vs equivalent committed VM cost)

I'll run an internal quick smoke on our side Monday and send the bench tar + instructions. If you can share a short sample payload (10 examples for chat, 1k vectors sample for embed), we'll pre-run models to provide an expected baseline.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks good and actionable. A few quick procurement/ops clarifications before we schedule the POC window:
1) Pricing: can you send a 6/12 month committed estimate (total committed spend and effective $/1M tokens) and an example of the delta if we need 2x burst for 4 hours/day? Procurement will need a clear representation of overage/burst billing.
2) SLA: we need a short doc that says what is guaranteed (uptime and concurrency) and what your rollback/fallback policy is — the SLA-comparison PDF is helpful, but procurement needs concrete language for the PO.
3) SOC2 & logs: send the SOC2 attestation link and explicit retention period for inference logs (we asked for 3 years). Also confirm location of KV cache (single-tenant in Dedicated deployments vs shared-tenant in hosted).

If you can provide those three items by EOD Friday (2/19), we'll schedule the POC kickoff for the week of 2/22 and loop procurement to issue a PO. I've attached procurement contacts in case you want to pre-seed a one-page commercial summary.

Thanks,
Asha
